decisions.reason: F6 cites only a quotient-field definition, which does not supply conjugation or modulus. Replaced that dependency and contract quotation with lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws, whose Statement supplies the exact additive, multiplicative and modulus identities. The tensor basis proof, finite-sum continuity, and conjugate-linear isometry J give the claimed representations with the first-variable-linear pairing; the Statement is unchanged.

With the library convention n starts at zero, U_0=(-1/0,1/0) is undefined. Reindexed both occurrences to U_n=(-1/(n+1),1/(n+1)), retaining the same cofinal shrinking neighbourhood argument. For each fixed x the shift t=x gives g(x-z)=g(-z) a.e.; convolution is then an integrable constant, hence zero, and right approximate-identity convergence forces g=0. This local indexing defect is nonfatal: no new mathematical argument or weakened claim is required.

F3 falsely states convolution for all continuous functions on an arbitrary G; f=g=1 on R makes the integral infinite. Every actual proof use is on compact K, where C(K)=C_c(K), so the cited convolution theorem applies. Restricted F3 to that compact case and removed unused general L2-convolution and norm claims. This is a nonfatal overstatement of a fact, not a gap in the separation argument: the symmetric cutoff gives psi(g)=0<psi(e), and spectral range orthogonality produces a finite-dimensional right-regular coefficient separating x and y.

F2 omitted the normalized-Haar hypothesis of the point-separation lemma, and the original proof never obtained that measure. Added cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group as a direct dependency and F4, then equipped K with its probability before applying F2. The existing AC assumption supplies Haar existence. Unitality, self-adjointness and point separation now meet Stone-Weierstrass exactly; epsilon/2 approximation gives sup error < epsilon. The Statement and all consumer interfaces are unchanged.

The cited Bochner definition requires an integrable-simple approximation and explicitly defers the finite-norm-integral criterion; the commuting-map theorem assumes integrability rather than proving it. Added the actual published criterion and integral norm inequality to F2, deps and contract. The finite-dimensional operator-valued integrand has measurable matrix entries, hence strong simple approximations, and integrable norm |f|. Its entries give <pi(f)e_j,e_i>=<f,u_ij>/sqrt(d_pi), so the Hilbert-Schmidt square sum, arbitrary-index Parseval and finite-subset-net inversion follow. The Statement is unchanged.
